title: Chapter 2 Quiz 5
description: Traps in every question. Several families look alike, so read each situation carefully.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: A program reads a number. If it is negative it displays an error and stops. Otherwise it displays the double of the number. Which family describes it best?
questions.explanation: The program takes a decision between two outcomes. Watch out: doubling a number is a linear step, but the decision makes the whole algorithm conditional.

questions.question: A function Fact(n) returns 1 when n = 0, and otherwise returns n × Fact(n - 1). Which family describes it best?
questions.explanation: The function calls itself on a smaller value. Watch out: it contains a test (n = 0), but the self-call is what defines recursion.

questions.question: Which of these tasks need **repetition** (an iterative algorithm)?
options: Printing each name in a list
Adding the two marks of one student
Choosing the larger of two marks
Summing every mark in a class
questions.explanation: Going through a whole collection needs a loop. Watch out: adding two marks is one step, and choosing the larger of two is a single decision.

questions.question: This loop should display the numbers 1 to 5. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Let i ← 1
While i < 5 Do
    Display(i)
    i ← i + 1
EndDo
questions.explanation: The last value, 5, must be displayed, so the test is i <= 5. Watch out: with i < 5 the loop stops after 4.

questions.question: This recursive function should return 1 + 2 + ... + n. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Function Sum(n) Returns integer
Begin
    If n = 0 Then
        Sum ← 0
    Else
        Sum ← n + Sum(n)
    EndIf
End Function
questions.explanation: The call must use a smaller value so that n reaches 0. Watch out: Sum(n) calls itself with the same value and never stops.

questions.assertion: A greedy algorithm always gives the best overall solution.
questions.reason: A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step.
questions.explanation: The assertion is false: the best choice at each step does not always give the best overall result. Watch out: the reason is true, and it is exactly why the assertion is tempting.

questions.question: Merge sort splits a list, sorts each half and merges the results. Which labels both apply?
questions.explanation: It is a sorting algorithm built on divide and conquer. Watch out: the labels are not exclusive, a single algorithm can belong to several families.

questions.question: Choose the best family for each situation.

rows.given: Double a number and display it
Check whether an age is valid
Add up all the elements of an array

questions.explanation: No decision, no repetition: linear. A decision: conditional. The same action for every element: iterative. A problem that contains smaller copies of itself: recursive. Watch out: folders inside folders look like a list, but the nesting calls for recursion.

questions.question: A recursive algorithm never needs a conditional test.
questions.explanation: A recursive function needs a test to know when to stop. Watch out: without a base case it would call itself for ever.

questions.question:
How many times does the body run?
```
For i From 2 To 9 Do
    Display(i)
EndDo
```
questions.explanation: i takes the values 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Watch out: both bounds are included, so it is 9 - 2 + 1 = 8, not 7.
